text: Debugging is a critical skill for any programmer. When your code doesn't work, the first step is identifying the bug—this means figuring out what the program is doing wrong and where the problem occurs. Instead of guessing, use a systematic approach: reproduce the error, isolate the faulty section, and test each possible cause one by one. Modern debugging tools make this easier. Breakpoints allow you to pause the program at specific lines and inspect variable values, while step-by-step execution shows you exactly what happens at each moment. Logging is another powerful method; by adding print statements or log messages, you can track the flow of data and see when things go off track. Remember that a patient, logical process will always beat random changes.
